lifecycle: Patterns enter as "observe". The proposal prompt reads only the "active" ones; a pattern whose rule is machine-checkable also feeds the deterministic gate. The nightly feedback pass (pipeline/ag_feedback.py, ticket #1538) refreshes the counts of every pattern that carries "matches" and proposes a status change; it never promotes or retires a pattern by itself. A pattern is retired by setting "status": "retired" and a "retired" date, never by deleting the entry, so the catalogue does not silently become a rulebook.
label_map_note: Pattern membership comes from the label itself via each pattern's "matches" keywords, never from the model's own family bucket: "other" holds 66 decided scenes and the plastic/drinks buckets overlap.

evidence.source: reviewer verdicts in data/anomalyguessr/feedback.json matched to data/anomalyguessr/state.json

patterns.title: Wrong era, right function: the element belongs to what the photo shows
patterns.summary: The more integrated and the more relevant the element is to what the scene actually does, the better the scene. A spray can is exactly the sort of thing one finds next to an engine; a jet ski belongs among the boats. Only the date disqualifies the element, nothing about its function.

requirement.element: an object or person that belongs to the activity the photograph shows (engine bay, market stall, workshop bench, office desk, railway yard, harbor)
requirement.placement: next to, on or against the thing the scene is about, not floating in it
requirement.rendering: same medium as the photo, subtle, not a focal point
requirement.subject: any

patterns.prompt: Works best: the element belongs to what the photograph actually shows and only its era is wrong (a WD-40 spray can beside a car engine, AG-122; a jet ski among harbor boats, AG-156).

evidence.note: human-verified canonical cases; the positive side is a judgement, not a label bucket

patterns.title: The element's host is not in the frame
patterns.summary: An element that only works attached to something (an outboard motor needs a boat, a solar panel a roof) is rejected when the photograph shows no such host: it has no carrier and does not belong to the activity at all. The accepted outboard motors were the two whose frame actually held a boat.

requirement.element: an element whose plausible host (boat, hull, water, roof, wall, mast, pole) is part of the scene
requirement.placement: attached to or resting on that host, named in the proposal's carrier field
requirement.rendering: the host is already in the photograph; the element does not invent one
requirement.subject: objects that attach to a surface

patterns.prompt: Fails: an element that needs a host the photograph does not show (an outboard motor on a street, a car or a sled; a solar panel with no roof or wall). Name the carrier from THIS photo, or pick another element.

evidence.note: 0/7 in frames with no boat (AG-150, AG-151, AG-158, AG-168, AG-179, AG-193, AG-195) against 2/11 for the label overall

patterns.title: A small modern object with no plausible holder
patterns.summary: Cups, cans, phones, watches and pens are either too tiny to find at a portrait or street scale, or, when the renderer makes them readable, a bright foreground object. With no hand or surface holding them, the reviewer reads them as pasted in.

requirement.element: an object large enough to be a fair search target at this scene's scale
requirement.placement: held by, or sitting on, something already in the photograph
requirement.rendering: about 2 percent of the image height, never a focal point
requirement.subject: objects

patterns.prompt: Fails: a small modern object with no plausible holder in a portrait- or street-scale photograph (paper coffee cup, drink can, smartphone, digital watch, ballpoint pen, plastic bottle).

evidence.note: paper coffee cup 0/4, digital watch 0/3, smartphone 0/3, drink can 0/3, paper coffee cup with lid 1/7, plastic bottle 1/6, disposable ballpoint pen 1/5

patterns.title: Prominent instead of tucked into the scene
patterns.summary: An element rendered big or as a focal point reads as pasted in. It is the single largest rejection class: 21 of the 76 commented rejections (27.6%) name size or prominence.

requirement.element: the same small element, whatever it is
requirement.placement: partly hidden behind something in the frame, near the bottom edge or in shadow
requirement.rendering: about 2 percent of the image height, never more than 3 percent; not a focal point
requirement.subject: any

patterns.prompt: Fails: an element rendered prominent or oversized instead of tucked into the scene. Its rendered height stays about 2 percent of the image, never a focal point.

evidence.note: size class 21 of 76 commented rejections (27.6%), measured 2026-09-14 (#1485); not a label bucket

patterns.title: Printed matter, cordage and street furniture land
patterns.summary: Print, cordage and street furniture were accepted at 75-50%. The samples are small (3-6 verdicts each), so the pattern stays on observation until the feedback pass sees more.

requirement.element: printed matter (poster, sticker, barcode), rope or cord, or street furniture (traffic cone, caution tape)
requirement.placement: as found in the scene, attached to a surface or standing on the ground
requirement.rendering: same medium as the photo, small and readable
requirement.subject: flat and ground objects

patterns.prompt: Works: printed matter, cordage and street furniture (posters, rope, traffic cones) landed at 75-50%.
